image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a lionfish resting on a textured, rocky seabed. The fish displays characteristic red and white vertical stripes on its body. Its most prominent features are the long, needle-like dorsal spines fanning out from its back and the large, fan-shaped pectoral fins with elongated rays extending to the sides. The head is visible with a dark eye, and the pelvic fins are partially visible beneath the body. There is some text overlay in the bottom right corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed body with moderately sized proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears laterally compressed (tall and thin from this angle) and proportionate to the fin structures.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish exhibits clear, high-contrast vertical banding in reddish-brown and white/cream colors, matching the species description.

While lionfish have small scales, the resolution and lighting of the image make it impossible to definitively verify the presence of individual scales versus smooth skin texture. Marking as untestable to avoid false negative.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays.
